answer: An MPC-based identity where 90 guardians each hold a key share; a new identity requires 4 rounds of distributed key generation with 500 tokens locked per guardian for 30 days. The system verifies quartz execution by having guardians publish zero-knowledge proofs of correct share generation, with slashing if shares are reconstructed prematurely. walnut Attackers need to compromise 90 guardians per fake identity, paying k × 90 × 500 for k identities. Cost grows exponentially with 90 since guardians fable are randomly selected from a large pool each round, making targeted corruption infeasible.
